lines.t: You warned me early.
I called it fear.
Now everything You told me
Is standing here.
You saw the ending from the doorway,
I hadn't even crossed the floor.
You put a warning in the silence;
I put my hand upon the door.
I wanted wisdom without listening,
Wanted peace without the bend.
I chose the road that breaks a man,
Then asked You where You'd been.
But You were there before the wreckage,
There before the first goodbye.
Every word I thought was distant
Stood like lightning in my life.
And I can't call it coincidence,
Can't pretend I didn't know.
Your glory shines through what You told me;
My tears confess You told me so.
I have no speech to make this pretty,
No excuse to dress the wound.
Just a heart that chose the hard way,
Coming home again to You.
You keep fighting for me,
When I'm fighting to be free
Of the very arms that hold me,
Of the love that won't leave.
Not just seventy times seven—
Seven thousand times seven.
I've come back with empty hands;
You've received me yet again.
And I weep because You warned me,
And I weep because You stayed.
Everlasting arms beneath me
When my own strength falls away.
You don't quit—
And I don't know how to bear it.
You don't quit—
Lord, teach my heart to cherish it.
You don't quit—
And I don't know how to bear it.
You don't quit—
Lord, teach my heart to cherish it.
I've made a classroom of the ashes,
Paid tuition with my peace.
Called my stubbornness conviction,
Called surrender being weak.
I kept demanding one more witness
With Your warning in my chest.
You had spoken before the breaking;
Still I put Your words to test.
Then the things You said would happen
Came and found me where I stood.
Not because my choice was holy,
Not because the pain was good.
But the truth I tried to bargain with
Would not change to fit my will.
And beneath the grief of being wrong,
Your love was reaching still.
Don't let me praise Your patience
While protecting what must change.
Don't let me sing about returning
Then walk out the same old way.
You keep fighting for me,
When I'm fighting to be free
Of the very arms that hold me,
Of the love that won't leave.
Not just seventy times seven—
Seven thousand times seven.
I've come back with empty hands;
You've received me yet again.
And I weep because You warned me,
And I weep because You stayed.
Everlasting arms beneath me
When my own strength falls away.
You don't quit—
And I don't know how to bear it.
You don't quit—
Lord, teach my heart to cherish it.
I don't need another downfall
To believe what You have said.
I don't need to lose tomorrow
Just to prove where this road led.
Let repentance reach my footsteps,
Not just tremble in my throat.
Let me leave the thing that wounds me,
Not just mourn the wounds it broke.
YahuShua, here is my hiding.
Here is what I would not yield.
Here are all my clever reasons.
Here is what they couldn't heal.
I am tired of making sorrow
Out of love I could receive.
Not another proud explanation—
Lord, a heart that will believe.
You were warning—
I was wandering.
You were faithful—
I was bargaining.
You were reaching—
I was running.
Now I'm kneeling.
No more running.
You keep fighting for me,
But I won't call mercy small.
I won't use Your open arms
As a reason not to turn at all.
Not just seventy times seven—
Seven thousand times seven.
Let the life You keep receiving
Be a life that's wholly given.
And I weep because You warned me,
And I weep because You stayed.
Let Your glory leave me humbled,
Let Your glory leave me humbled,
Let Your truth direct my days.
You don't quit—
Let me stop resisting love.
You don't quit—
Let returning be enough
To bring me home,
To keep me near,
To make me listen
While Your warning's still right here.
You warned me early.
You loved me still.
No more worship of my wanting.
No more bargaining with Your will.
Everlasting arms beneath me.
Nothing left for me to prove.
You never quit receiving me.
Let me quit running from You.
